transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I just can't shake this thought I keep having. I'm an electrician, have been for years. But if all those years of doing this couldn't keep my own brother safe... then I just figure I'm a danger to anybody who works with me. Or even the people living under my roof. I just had to talk to somebody about it.
I'm very sorry to hear that. Could you tell me what happened with your brother?

It was an accident on a job site. We were working together and... well, things went wrong. I was supposed to be the experienced one, the one making sure everything was secure. 

I honestly can't bring myself to go through the exact details of it right now. It's just... my mind kind of shuts down when I try to explain it. He got hurt, and it happened on my watch. That's... that's really all I can say about it today.
How long ago did the accident happen?
It was about four months ago. This has all been going on ever since the garage fire... and my nephew coming to live with us.
Do unwanted memories or images of the accident repeatedly pop into your mind when you don't want them to?

Yeah, they do. All the time. I'll just be... I'll be in the middle of wiring a panel at work, or even just hearing my nephew shut the garage door at home. And suddenly I'm right back there. I can actually smell the smoke, and I see my brother. It's like the whole job site just drops out from under me.
Since the accident, have you felt constantly on guard, jumpy, or easily startled?

No, not really. I mean, I'm stressed, sure, but I wouldn't say I'm constantly on guard or jumping at every little thing. It's more just... the memories popping up like I mentioned. But as for being jumpy, no, I haven't really noticed that.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in activities you normally enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I still like the things I usually do. I still like going fishing when I get the chance, and watching the game on Sundays. It's just hard to find the time right now with my nephew here, but I haven't lost interest in them or anything.
Do you find yourself going out of your way to avoid certain places, people, or situations that remind you of the accident?

Yeah, I do. Um... for one, I don't go in my own garage anymore unless I absolutely have to. I also quit helping out with the electrical stuff down at the church. And... well, if anyone starts talking about car projects, or the fire, I just shut them down fast. I just don't want any part of those conversations.
Have you been having trouble falling or staying asleep since the accident?

Yeah, sleep has been really rough. Most nights I just lie there in bed, kind of... listening, I guess. Waiting to hear a crackling sound or a car door shutting in the driveway. And when I finally do manage to fall asleep, I end up jolting awake, just completely soaked in sweat from dreaming about the garage. Once that happens, I can't get back to sleep before I have to get up for work.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets diagnostic criteria for post-traumatic stress disorder (F43.1) following a traumatic workplace accident/garage fire 4 months ago resulting in severe injury to his brother. He exhibits classic symptoms across core clusters including intrusive re-experiencing (flashbacks, olfactory and visual intrusions, distressing nightmares), behavioral avoidance (avoiding the garage, electrical work at church, and conversations about the event), negative cognitions regarding personal blame/guilt, and arousal symptoms (sleep disturbances and nocturnal vigilance), with symptoms persisting well beyond the one-month mark.

Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs about oneself and guilt regarding responsibility for the accident
Sleep disturbance with difficulty falling and staying asleep, nocturnal alertness listening for sounds
